reviews.review:
Pro: Lots of fun
Con: Multiplayer is dead as hell

Shallow and practically empty.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The SEARCHING FOR FIRETEAM screen has a short music loop which tries to convey tension, but you have to wait so long to get a teammate that it gets annoyingly repetitive. I went over the 2 hour refund window while waiting the best part of an hour (during peak time) to find a teammate, and when a teammate finally arrived (and the game gave us a bot to fill the 3rd slot) the game then crashed on loading. I wish I had stopped and got a refund. Having passed the 2 hour mark, I tried to get some sense of value for money by waiting for teammates and attempting to complete the game, but it was mostly just waiting, or getting stuck due to artificial difficulty. It's possible to start a mission with bots by making a private lobby, but this isn't obvious, the bots are pretty useless, and players won't be able to drop in.

For the little time I had a teammate, there was little to no teamwork involved. I didn't hear any mic chat, and couldn't find a button for text chat. The scale of the game feels limited with only two teammates. The weapons don't feel like they suit any particular role, range, or circumstance. The pulse rifle fire rate feels wrong, and has no grenade launcher. Weapon switch and reload animations, and sounds are poor. The game didn't need hitmarkers; there's a big red X that appears when you kill an Alien, was it worth throwing away immersion for that? Many maps feel boringly modular. Bizarrely your hitpoints are counted at 1,500 which didn't give me a sense of vulnerability like having it counted by 100 would.

Sometimes there's a bunch of mines in your path, which adds nothing to the gameplay. It's just tedious switching to your pistol that has unlimited ammo to shoot all the mines. A lot of the game feels like that - stuff being added even if it doesn't contribute positively to gameplay. Some enemies are bullet sponges, which doesn't make the gameplay feel skill-based, and isn't fun considering the lack of ammunition. The difficulty ramps up ridiculously as you get swarmed by bullet sponge enemies that deal high damage (and some have ranged attacks, but there's no button to crouch, so taking cover is janky). To beat the bullet sponges you would have to grind earlier missions to make your character slightly more powerful (or wait ages hoping to get a powerful teammate).

[h1]General confusion[/h1]
There's kit perks, core perks, modifiers, [i]"tactical opportunities"[/i], abilities, cards, attachments, intel, rep, requisition, weapon upgrade traits, [i]"daily opportunity"[/i] (fear of missing out?) Ontop of XP, ranks, and consumables. There's popups for challenge cards as soon as you launch the game, and some perks can be rotated to fit into a confusing inventory system that increases [i]"combat rating"[/i], different from the primary inventory menu. Did it all have to be this complicated, as opposed to polishing core gameplay?

[h1]Poor quality[/h1]
The higher FPS options are either 120 or unlocked, which wastes electricity when you consider it has a 3D menu, and you wait so long to get matched with teammates. For some reason there's also a 2D menu (reached from ESC), and weirdly it all moves as you move the cursor. The cosmetics for changing outfits didn't show a preview of the character on my client, and they look ridiculous. One player looked like they were wearing Valentines Day gift wrapping rather than camouflage. The water droplets and fires are low framerate effects, and many effects flicker. There's no ripple effect when shooting water. The game suffers microstutters. There's no ambient motion tracker ping, and the tracker fails to pick up a lot of motion. The voicelines are poor. There's a damage increase HUD element that comes up and felt pointless. Private matches can't be paused.

[h1]Story[/h1]
The theme of flame and explosive weapons in the wider lore were chaotic ones that were deployed as a desperate last resort. Here they're thrown straight into combat. A character claims that humans never encountered a tool-using civilization. Did the devs not even watch the Aliens movie? They mention a species called the Arcturians, and encounter a massive alien ship at the start. What I assume was supposed to be a plot twist doesn't even feel like a spoiler because [spoiler]it happens in every Aliens game[/spoiler] when [spoiler]some synthetics are hostile.[/spoiler]

Between missions you're supposed to listen to NPCs waffle on, meanwhile I'm worried that my teammates are waiting for me to join the next mission. Couldn't the devs have layered the story into the gameplay like in AVP2? The characters are edgy and forgettable with no range of personality. There's no sense of camaraderie between the enlisted, and officers have no command presence. One officer that spends the entire game just standing in one spot shouts at you [i]"What? What! Do I look like I have time to chatter?"[/i] There's no humour in the voiceline, so it doesn't come across with any hint of sarcasm. In the film the leaders were more 3-dimensional, either inexperienced but authoritative, or bossy but still had a hint of charisma.

The story butchers [spoiler]the corruption dynamic by characters doing unquestionably immoral things, whereas the film was subtle with deniability. Where's the incentive for the military to fight for these corrupt entities in a post-scarcity civilisation? They either wouldn't bother to fight, or would just lose all motivation to enlist or re-enlist. One character says they don't have to, so why do they do it?[/spoiler]

Aliens was largely about the Aliens - the development here should have looked for creative ways to show their ruthlessness and the intelligence of these emotionless creatures to contrast the moral flaws in society. Yet the aliens are left so stupid in this game that they can literally get stuck while trying to move towards you. They don't work together, they just get spammed, but the ship crew complements are so low in the lore that it doesn't make sense to be killing thousands of Aliens. Where are they all coming from? I didn't see anything that justified the scale of their numbers. The development should have added quality to the encounters with them, then they wouldn't even need to spam them. The Aliens in AVP (1999) were more tangible and had weight to them - when you shot them they'd lose limbs and menacingly still crawl and swiped at you, and bled far more dangerous acid in concentrations, not just splashed like momentary stains.

[h1]Summary[/h1]
This feels like a cash-grab, where the only effort was put into graphics to make it look good in a trailer to get pre-orders (made obvious by the pre-order bonus system). You can't just jam some NPCs into a series of corridors and call it a sci-fi story. AVP (1999) had a lot of this nonsense beat 22 years earlier. It sounded better, had better Aliens, had NPC mouth movement, and GameSpy enabled you to see every lobby so you could immediately jump into a multiplayer match. As much as I liked Aliens and drew my nickname from it, I didn't find the gameplay enjoyable in this instalment to even want to complete it. The difficulty ramps up to the point where you'd need to grind previous missions to upgrade a character to survive later missions. I'd rather watch a film.

There's so little teamwork involved that I wouldn't recommend it to my friends, which is ironic because it's a Left 4 Dead clone that should have been all about trying to flesh out satisfying teamwork. This game is not worth £34.99, and the pricetag only acts as a paywall to the players it needs as teammates. Unimaginative cash-grabs like this are the reason that Aliens games never got anywhere near as popular as Halo. There was no effort in places where it mattered. I can only imagine a sense of value for money if it was heavily discounted, but honestly you could just skip this one.

Game is Fun but has a short story/campaign. Definitely more fun with friends then playing solo but i enjoyed doing both. All the classes are pretty unique from one another and i only found myself not enjoying 1 of the 6 you can pick from. "Phalanx was my least favorite class" Its hard to pick my favorite because i really enjoy all 4 of theses the same "Technician, Recon, Gunner and Demolisher" Doc was fun to play too but i feel its healing is lacking. "The overall class is lacking in how a healer class roll should be"

The Perk system is pretty cool and is my type of personal customization i look for in a game that allows you to make different builds. However, its a bit shallow. Needs work but its at least good enough to play the game and sink a couple hundred hours into try things out before you realize there isn't many options.

Visually the game looks great and the AI/NPC enemies are well done. "really fun shooting those aliens" But the animation on your character is definitely not AAA animation. Especially the movement. Shooting on the other hand feels great as well as your abilities/skills. If they could touch up the movement animation it would be a huge improvement in the overall feel of the game when playing.

If you watch any gameplay on this game before you buy it, expect exactly what you see. There isnt any hidden gems here. Its a fun game to play....finish....rank up all the classes......then move on and wait for the next update or DLC. Though i will say there are a couple side game modes you could play after you dont all the above but its not going to keep your attention too long. There is Probably ~200 Hours worth of playtime in Alien fireteam elite if you're one that completes everything.

None the less i had fun.
